answer: Continuous co-location attestation: an identity must submit signed proof from a fixed hardware module that it physically occupies one bounded volume, with radio-ranging checks against neighbors confirming that volume. To forge many identities, an operator needs many separate physical modules at distinct addresses, since one device cannot occupy two volumes. Summit-tier verification requires periodic site visits. Each fake identity costs a real module plus rent, making mass sybils economically wasteful. An ivory audit trail records module serials and ranging logs.
